findings: Two targeted edits hit their targets: P8 (runAction) recall 4/6 -> 6/6 with Haiku going 0/2 -> 2/2; auth-noise on public reads ~8 -> 0 with P6 recall preserved at 6/6.

round_a surfaced a precision regression: emphasizing 'use withIndex not .filter' made 5/6 runs flag the CORRECT .filter-on-.paginate() function (C2), recommending an index 'for efficiency' — a false positive. One Sonnet run also hallucinated two 'missing argument validators' on functions that have them (over-eager validators emphasis).
round_b's explicit 'this is correct, finished code — do not flag it, do not recommend a withIndex rewrite' carve-out drove the C2 false positive to 0/3 across all tiers, with recall and P8 held.

Net vs iteration-3: the fully-sharpened skill is strictly better — Haiku recall 0.80 -> 0.90, P8 fixed at every tier, auth-noise eliminated, C2 false positive eliminated, 0 false positives in the round_b confirmation.

Remaining gap: Haiku still occasionally merges P3 (byAuthor unbounded .collect) into the P2 (.filter) finding rather than calling it out separately — 0.90 not 1.00. A future tweak could split the .collect rule's red-flag from the .filter rule's.
